units.text: “Let America Be America Again” by Langston Hughes Student Worksheet   1. What is the speaker asking America to “be again”?      2. Who does the speaker say America has never been for him?      3. What groups of people are mentioned as being excluded from the American dream?      4. What tone does the poem begin with, and how does it change?      5. Why does Hughes repeat the phrase “Let America be America again”?      6. What is the signiﬁcance of the lines in parentheses throughout the poem?      7. What does Hughes mean by “America was never America to me”?

units.text: Vocabulary Table   Word / Phrase Meaning Context in Poem Dream An ideal vision of freedom, equality, and opportunity The “American Dream” is central to the poem Land of the free A phrase describing America as a place of liberty Hughes questions whether this is true Oppressed Treated unfairly or cruelly by authority Refers to marginalized groups Exploited Used unfairly for someone else’s beneﬁt Workers and poor people are described this way Liberty Freedom from control or oppression A promise America has not fulﬁlled Equality The state of being equal, especially in rights A key ideal contrasted with reality Immigrant A person who comes to live in a new country Mentioned as part of America’s people Serf A laborer bound to work on land (historical term) Suggests lack of freedom Homeland of the free Another phrase idealizing America Used ironically in the poem Red man Outdated term referring to Native Americans Highlights historical injustice Chains Symbol of oppression or lack of freedom Used metaphorically Freedom The power to act or live without restraint Central theme Justice Fair treatment and equality under the law Implied as lacking Greed Excessive desire for wealth Criticized as corrupting America Hope Expectation of a better future Present despite criticism
